pretreatments.description: Knife milling (KM): A mechanical pretreatment involving a milling chamber with mobile milling elements mounted on a central shaft that apply forces to disaggregate solid particles, slice fibers, and produce small pieces (similar to chopping with a knife). This treatment is typically used for substrates with total solids content higher than 85%.

Hammer mill (HM): A mechanical pretreatment consisting of a rotor with a set of attached hammers that impact the material against a breaker plate when the rotor turns, grinding the fibers into long and thin pieces. This technology grinds fibers similarly to a mortar and pestle.

Extruder (EX): A mechanical pretreatment where raw materials are fed into one end of the system and transported along the length of the barrel with a driving screw. The material moves along the barrel, undergoing friction heat, mixing, and vigorous shearing upon pressure release at the finishing end.

Shredding + hydrodynamic cavitation (SHC): A combined pretreatment system where a wet shredder with integrated heavy material separator homogenizes fluids, protecting downstream hydrodynamic cavitation components from damage. The hydrodynamic cavitation reactor uses a stator and rotor assembly to generate cavitation bubbles for the generation, growth, and collapse of microbubbles in the digestate.
